"snapcn Pro" shrinks away, a cluster of screens flies at the camera and opens into a wall of snapcn components, the wall drifts and then whips aside to reveal the first word already sliding in, and the page cuts to "One subscription." then "Endless videos." — each second word landing as the first one moves over. The wall is 32 screens on their own measured tracks (a single 3D camera fits it to 2.7–6.7px, so none is used), with the fly-in cards drawn from their four corners because they are turned in depth; the lines are drawn at 4–8x and averaged down so a zoom of a quarter pixel a frame stays smooth. Built frame by frame against a screen recording: 4.6 of 255 mean per pixel over all 97 captures, 1.1–1.3 on the type.
items.docs: Docs and props: https://snapcn.dev/docs/scenes/library-flight?ref=cli — title is the opening card beside the snapcn mark; first and second are the two lines, each split at its first space into the word that arrives and the word that lands. images takes ;-separated URLs handed to the screens back to front (snapcn's posters by default); devices=false stretches each picture over its screen instead of framing it as a laptop, tablet or window. background and color are the page and the type.

items.name: wire-feed
items.title: Wire Feed
items.description: News feed animation: a live changelog feed typing its newest item as the camera pulls back. A live feed writing its newest item while the camera pulls back. Close on a title, a source types itself in beside a caret, its age fades up sliding into place and a rule draws out beneath it; then a cut to the wide shot seconds later, the headline most of the way written, as two older items slide in from the right out of a blur, nineteen frames apart, every age ticking up, the camera still easing out and drifting left as it ends. The camera, the typing, the caret, the fade, the rule and both entrances are replayed from tables measured frame by frame off a 60fps screen recording, and every line is placed with a transform rather than flow so a sub-pixel layout survives the zoom: 1.20 of 255 mean per pixel across 156 captures once the recording's blur is matched, 0.32 on the close shot. Ships as a snapcn changelog — pass your own copy and it re-wraps, re-stacks and types on the recording's frames.
items.docs: Docs and props: https://snapcn.dev/docs/scenes/wire-feed?ref=cli — title, source1-3, age1-3, headline1-3 and body2-3 are the copy; headline1 is the one typed live. Paints its own near-white page; the colour props cover every ink and caretColor is the accent.

items.name: pack-up
items.title: Pack Up
items.description: Typewriter text animation into a 3D box: a headline types, then its words are packed into a cardboard carton. A line types itself, catches the light, and its last word is packed into a box. The sentence arrives one character per frame, each landing in the accent and cooling to the text colour behind a caret that never blinks, with a single five-frame hold after the first word that is the whole rhythm of the open. Then a highlight crosses the finished line — not a fade: every letter it touches is pushed up through the accent until almost nothing of it is left, and comes back down behind it. Then the line breaks. The leading words accelerate out of frame to the left, under constant acceleration onto a terminal speed, while the last word stays, rocks four frames backwards, and only then tips forward as an open slotted carton swings up from the bottom right — wider than the frame — and settles. A second copy of the word is thrown in from off frame to meet it, and the near flap passes in front of both as they go in: the carton is projected in this file rather than handed to CSS 3D precisely so that paint order is exact. The typing rate, the highlight's profile, the break-out curve, the tumble, the carton's seven shape parameters and its whole camera path are measured tables on a 30fps reference's own frame grid.
items.docs: Docs and props: https://snapcn.dev/docs/scenes/pack-up?ref=cli — pass headline for the line that types itself (its last word is the one that falls into the box), copies for how many go in, accent for the colour a character arrives in and the caret, and carton for the box's lit paper, which defaults to your card surface. capHeight, tracking, shape and beats are there for when the copy is not fifteen characters long.

items.name: task-stream
items.title: Task Stream
items.description: AI agent task list animation: steps stream in with spinners and tick off. An agent's task list, streaming in and ticking off. A heading writes itself a word at a time and a chevron lands after it; a spinner slides in and each task streams in beside it, every word fading up as it drifts into place. A band of blue sweeps through the line while the task runs, then the spinner flashes into a glowing check that draws itself, cools from cyan to blue and settles into ink before the next task starts. The shot opens close on the first task and pulls back to the whole list as the work gets going. Replayed from a 60fps screen recording measured frame by frame: the camera, the rail, every word's arrival and the check's flash are tables and fitted curves, not taste.
items.docs: Docs and props: https://snapcn.dev/docs/ai-input/task-stream?ref=cli — 60fps. Pass title for the heading and steps (up to five) for the tasks; accent, shimmerColor, flashColor and glowColor paint the running task and its check, speed scales the whole timeline.

items.name: glass-prompt
items.title: Glass Prompt
items.description: AI prompt animation: a glass prompt bar, a send click and a dive into a ring of results. A prompt typed into a pane of glass, and a dive through its send button into the ring of pictures it asked for. A glass pill floats over rolling hills and the request types itself in; an arrow pops in at its end. The shot cuts in close on the arrow with the hills gone soft behind the glass, a pointer rises to it and presses, and the pane rolls and rushes the lens — the arrow swelling into a band of light, the glass washing out to white — until the camera is through it and nine pictures fan out of the arrow's middle into a ring, each one developing out of a blue negative into its own colours as the ring comes round. Replayed from a 4.1s screen recording measured frame by frame: the camera is an affine per frame, the roll a similarity fitted on the pill's own edges, the glass a fixed window onto a small copy of the backdrop, and every tile tracked from its final rect.
items.docs: Docs and props: https://snapcn.dev/docs/ai-input/glass-prompt?ref=cli — 151 frames at 30fps. prompt (a long one shrinks to fit the glass), backdrop (empty draws hills), images or image1…image9 for the ring, fontFamily and textScale; frost, rim and lensZoom for the glass; focus and motionBlur for the camera; showPointer, pointer and pointerFill; ringScale, ringBlur and tileRadius; print and printDark/Mid/Light for the blue negative; background and speed. Also installs into Remotion Studio from the gallery, with every prop in the Inspector.

items.name: pain-point
items.title: Pain Point
items.description: Launch video intro: a typed question as the camera pulls back through floating UI cards. The opening beat of a launch video: the viewer's pain, typed as a question, while the camera pulls back through the tools they are stuck in. A violet glow blooms out of black, the first line types itself with its newest characters running from white to violet, the camera dollies back and nine UI cards cut in at their own depths, a second line takes over, and the camera rushes back in. Replayed from a 4.5s screen recording measured frame by frame: a single dollying camera solved from nine tracked cards (0.26% scale error), the glow as fitted super-gaussian blobs, the type fitted for size, weight and tracking, and every reveal frame read off the capture.
items.docs: Docs and props: https://snapcn.dev/docs/scenes/pain-point?ref=cli — 136 frames at 30fps. `lines` is the question in two beats; `cards` takes your own UI for the nine planes.

items.name: template-launch
items.title: Launch Video Template
items.description: A finished product-launch video in five beats — hook, product, proof, numbers, wordmark — on one paper with a dissolve between each. Type your words and colours once in LAUNCH_CONTENT; every beat reads them. Each beat lists the components you can swap in, with the command that installs them.

items.name: search-retype
items.title: Search Retype
items.description: A search field types its first query, the camera pushes in, the query deletes back to nothing and a new one types in. Every keystroke, deletion and caret blink lands on the frame it did in the reference recording; each new character arrives in the accent and settles to ink, and the field leaves on a sideways whip.

items.name: ember-reveal
items.title: Ember Reveal
items.description: Glow text reveal animation: a brush sweeps across and blooms into a glow that writes the line. A brush of colour sweeps across a blush backdrop, curls up and flicks back on itself, then blooms into a soft glow that writes the line right to left, the letters warm where the glow is hottest, before the line sinks into place under a soft halo. Blue by default; the recording's orange-on-blush is a few props away. Replayed from a screen recording measured frame by frame: the brush's centre line, width and end fades, the glow's shape and strength, the line's drift and settle, every letter's arrival and the backdrop are fitted tables.

items.name: spark-question
items.title: Spark Question
items.description: Kinetic typography question: a headline asked phrase by phrase, each landing huge as sparkles dart past. A question asked one phrase at a time: each phrase lands huge and settles while the camera keeps pulling back, its words blurring up into place one after another as small four-point sparkles dart past, and a hard cut swaps in the next. The last phrase lands over a soft circle backdrop whose rings drift outward. Timing and geometry are measured frame by frame off a screen recording: every phrase's ink box, the pull-back and each sparkle's flight are fitted tables.

items.name: blueprint-collage
items.title: Blueprint Collage
items.description: Photo collage animation: pictures hop around a cycling headline, then clear to the last word. A headline cycles through three phrases while five pictures and a disc hop around it in 15fps stop motion, the camera eases back, and the pictures clear away one by one to leave the last phrase fading from the accent to ink. Every picture's pose is fitted frame by frame off a screen recording.
items.docs: Docs and props: https://snapcn.dev/docs/scenes/blueprint-collage?ref=cli — 56 frames at 30fps. phrases, images, accent, ink, background, mode, theme and speed.

items.name: prompt-roll
items.title: Prompt Roll
items.description: A prompt card is pushed in on while "Make your own …" types, cuts closer, and the last words wrap into a pill that rolls through what you can make, each in its own tint. The sentence finishes, the camera whips to a send button that draws itself in, a pointer presses it into a halo, and the arrow pulls free and flies off as the frame washes to white. Replayed from a 6.4s screen recording measured frame by frame: the push-in's card rect, the tracked pan, every keystroke, each roll step, the pointer's path and the press.

items.name: dot-dissolve
items.title: Dot Dissolve
items.description: LED dot-matrix transition: dots pop in across the frame in clumps until the matrix covers it, hold, then break up in clumps and let go, the last stragglers out bottom left. Each dot takes its tone off a drifting noise field mapped onto a calm dusk palette (slate, dusty blue, mist), so the matrix drifts like soft light through LEDs. It paints only its dots, so it lays over any cut: cut between your shots under it at DOT_DISSOLVE_CUT.
items.docs: Docs and props: https://snapcn.dev/docs/transitions/dot-dissolve?ref=cli — 38 frames at 30fps. Lay it over both shots and cut under it at DOT_DISSOLVE_CUT (frame 16). columns, palette, gap, seed and speed.

items.name: mark-grid
items.title: Mark Grid
items.description: App icon grid animation: a headline types around your logo, then a wall of app icons opens round it. The last scene wipes away and a line types itself in around your mark, lifts off word by word, and a staggered wall of tiles opens round the mark as the camera eases in. A dozen app icons fade into the wall and three name pills rise in beside them. The face, camera, wipe and every fade are measured off a screen recording.

items.name: pixel-peak
items.title: Pixel Peak
items.description: Pixel transition: the next shot climbs through the last as a stepped peak of blocks. Transition for @remotion/transitions: the next shot climbs up through the last one as a stepped peak of blocks. A 20 × 10 grid opens at the bottom middle, widens and climbs, its edge flickering with single frames of blue before each block cuts to the next shot; the top corners go last. Every block's flash frame, cut frame and colour is replayed from a screen recording (all 37 frames within 1.42/255). Only the transition: your two shots are the scenes either side of it in a TransitionSeries.

Replayed from a screen recording fitted on every frame: each picture's rect, each fade, the camera, the lens and the flash (all 56 recorded frames within 5.9/255, mean 3.4).

Timing, glide and shake are measured frame by frame off a screen recording.
